_note: Evergreen editorial seed pool for retrofuturism, written by Claude on 2026-11-05 for owner review. Tips, ideas, real tools (homepage links only) and generic opportunities. No news: news only comes from the brand's listed feeds. Edit freely.

items.title: Look up the futures people once imagined
items.summary: Old predictions show what we valued.

items.title: Sketch your city as it would be if it kept the best of the past
items.summary: Then check what is already possible.

items.title: Ask what a tool does with your data before you adopt it
items.summary: Read the privacy page for ten minutes. It tells you the real price.

items.title: Read the abstract and conclusion before the headline
items.summary: Most hype lives in the gap between the two.

items.title: Test a new tool on a task you already know well
items.summary: You can judge the result when you know what good looks like.

items.title: Build a tiny project with a tool you do not understand yet
items.summary: A weekend project teaches more than a month of reading.

items.title: Collect predictions from ten years ago and score them
items.summary: It is humbling and it sharpens your view of today's claims.

items.title: Ask an expert in another field how they use the same technology
items.summary: Different fields find different uses.

items.title: Hugging Face
items.summary: A hub for open machine-learning models and datasets.

items.title: arXiv
items.summary: Free preprints of research papers in science and computing.

items.title: Our World in Data
items.summary: Charts and data on global problems and progress.

items.title: Join an open-source project
items.summary: Documentation fixes are a friendly first contribution.

items.title: Visit a maker space or hack night
items.summary: Hands-on tinkering beside people who like the same things.

items.title: Look at one artwork for ten full minutes
items.summary: Past the first reaction, a picture keeps giving.

items.title: Visit a gallery on its quiet day
items.summary: You can stand where you like and look as long as you like.

items.title: Start a small collection of postcards or prints
items.summary: Cheap, personal and a good reason to visit museum shops.

items.title: Trade a drawing a week with a friend
items.summary: A low-pressure habit that adds up.

items.title: Google Arts & Culture
items.summary: Explore artworks and exhibitions from museums around the world.

items.title: Europeana
items.summary: Millions of digitized artworks, books and recordings from European institutions.

items.title: Volunteer at a gallery or arts festival
items.summary: Volunteers see behind the scenes and often get free entry.
